A1.justification: Both PDFs describe V-REX. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and appendix additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 32 VLMs, including planning and following accuracy, failure recovery, correlations, and qualitative cases.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds image-free evaluation, expanded-choice planning experiments, and shared-failure analyses.

M1.justification: The CoQ planning/following procedures and two-stage distractor-generation pipeline remain unchanged. Revised generation-prompt documentation does not establish a changed algorithm or regenerated benchmark.

E1.justification: The benchmark retains 702 samples, 2,504 questions, four categories, and 15 scenarios. Appendix F adds evaluation without input images, extending coverage to a missing-visual-input scenario without introducing new datasets or domains.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain all 32 VLMs in Tables 1 and 3 and the same 12 models in Table 2. New analyses use subsets of these existing models under additional conditions, without introducing new comparison methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds image-free evaluation of 17 models, four-versus-eight-option planning evaluation of 19 models, and a six-model shared-failure protocol with difficulty stratification and a 75% failure threshold. These substantially extend the evaluation design; the original experiments' stated settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendices F, G, and I test visual dependence, sensitivity to planning-option count, and whether different models fail at common reasoning steps. These substantially extend v1's existing recovery analysis and case studies, which are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run or seed counts, and v2 adds no confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure. Existing correlation significance reporting is retained; the new shared-failure fractions are diagnostic metrics rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All model scores in Tables 1–3 are unchanged. New Tables 4–5 and Figures 12–13 add substantial results: for example, Table 5 reports GPT-5 planning averages of 84.44% with four options and 55.79% with eight. Appendix I additionally reports 69 hard Following samples and 43 hard Planning samples.

T1.justification: Appendix I introduces mathematical difficulty definitions using AvgCorrect and UnanimousFail: easy requires perfect intermediate accuracy, while hard requires a unanimously failed step or accuracy below 0.5. Original CoQ equations and chain-validity conditions remain unchanged; no proofs or theorems are added.

C1.justification: The benchmark contribution, separation of planning and following, five headline findings, and conclusion are retained. Rewording planning and explicitly identifying CoQ as evaluation rather than performance-enhancing prompting clarify the existing contribution without changing its scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation of benchmark validity and difficulty. Appendix F identifies Navigation's unusually strong image-free performance and possible textual shortcuts; G discusses candidate-count sensitivity and broadly stable rankings; I interprets shared failure peaks as grounding and integration bottlenecks and remaining benchmark headroom.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 revises documented distractor-generation instructions and abbreviates output schemas. References also newly provide direct access links for the GeoGuessr and TimeGuessr sources. Hardware, model-access arrangements, evaluation prompts, and the project link are retained.

R1.justification: The introduction adds an explicit distinction between CoQ evaluation and CoT-style prompting, providing a limited positioning clarification. The cited works and related-work discussion otherwise remain the same; expanded bibliography metadata does not introduce new research.

P1.justification: Existing prose is largely preserved. Local changes include abstract and introduction clarification, author-information updates, a short Additional Results subsection, revised prompt wording, and replacement of numbered appendices and their contents page with lettered appendices.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the two-column main layout with a single-column format and extensively resizes and relocates exhibits. Figures 4 and 6 rearrange stacked panels horizontally, while two tables and two shared-failure figures are added. Earlier case-study figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Appendices F, G, and I strengthen the existing benchmark study through visual-dependence controls, option-count sensitivity tests, and shared-failure diagnostics. Explicitly acknowledging Navigation's textual cues improves interpretation. These supporting gains provide a positive but limited overall improvement; compressed exhibits and unfinished running headers slightly reduce presentation quality.
